solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: A calf I massaged in cosmetic treatment (6)

indicatorNotes.massaged: massaging works something over, so the letters are kneaded into a new order

annotation.surface: A beauty salon session where a leg rub is thrown in with the face treatment.
annotation.walkthrough: The massage talk sounds like part of the spa scene, but it is only telling you to rearrange the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the noun facial names a salon treatment of the face, the kind of cosmetic treatment the clue means.

entries.clue: Intended to work in cafe (6)

indicatorNotes.to work: letters put to work are set in motion and moved into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone meant to take a job at a café.
annotation.walkthrough: "Intended" reads as a verb (meant to), but it is the noun: one's intended is the person one is engaged to.
annotation.definitionFit: A fiancé is the person you intend to marry, your intended.

entries.clue: Bird bites as nip infuriated dog (6,7)

indicatorNotes.bites: something that bites takes another thing between its jaws, so COCKEREL holds the other letters
indicatorNotes.infuriated: an infuriated thing is stirred up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: AS and NIP rearranged, then placed inside COCKER...EL

annotation.surface: A bird pecks at an angry dog, which then gets nipped.
annotation.walkthrough: The bird is not the answer's COCK alone: the whole COCKEREL splits around the rearranged letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the cocker spaniel is one particular breed, and the clue names only its broad class.

entries.clue: Sneeze in a sneeze catcher, did you say? (7)

indicatorNotes.did you say?: asks whether we heard it right, so the answer is what the words sound like when spoken

annotation.surface: Someone mishears a sneeze into a hanky.
annotation.walkthrough: ATISHOO is the British spelling of the sneeze noise (American: achoo). Say "a tissue" quickly and it sounds the same.
annotation.definitionFit: Atishoo is the sound of a sneeze, used as a word for one.

entries.clue: Sporting figure in Lord’s hat? (6)

blocks.note: the player who delivers the ball at cricket

annotation.surface: A question about a lord's headwear, as if a sportsman lived in it.
annotation.walkthrough: Lord's is the London cricket ground, not a nobleman; the apostrophe tempts you to read "a lord's hat".
annotation.definitionFit: A bowler bowls at cricket, and a bowler is a hard round hat.

entries.clue: Greek character, old and big (5)

annotation.surface: A description of a large, elderly Greek person.
annotation.walkthrough: "Character" sounds like a person, but it means a letter of the alphabet.
annotation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet.

entries.clue: Place for dirty habits? (7,6)

blocks.note: reads as a haunt or den; really a container that holds things
reads as vices; really soiled garments, habit as in a nun's habit

annotation.surface: A den of vice where bad habits are indulged.
annotation.walkthrough: "Dirty habits" suggests vices; read habits as garments and the dirty ones go in the wash basket.
annotation.definitionFit: A laundry basket is where soiled clothes are kept before washing.

entries.clue: Tell English story about being led by king (6)

indicatorNotes.about: turning about faces the other way, so the letters run backwards
indicatorNotes.being led by: what is led follows its leader, so R comes first

blocks.note: E for English plus TALE, then turned round to ELATE

annotation.surface: Instructions to recount an English tale about a monarch.
annotation.walkthrough: "About" looks like it means "concerning"; here it turns E + TALE round.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the storytelling sense: you relate or tell an anecdote, not the sense of being connected.

entries.clue: Vault I have for record collection (7)

annotation.surface: Someone owns a strongroom to keep their vinyl in.
annotation.walkthrough: "Vault" suggests a strongroom, but here it is the architectural sense: an arched ceiling.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: documents kept for history make up the store the clue calls a record collection, nothing to do with vinyl.

entries.clue: One going in deep next, where swimming appropriate (9)

indicatorNotes.going in: one thing goes in among the others, so I sits inside
indicatorNotes.swimming: letters swimming about are moving freely, so they land in a new order

blocks.note: Roman numeral one, placed inside after EXPED

annotation.surface: A swimmer jumps into the deep end, where swimming is fitting.
annotation.walkthrough: The deep end of a pool is the scene, but "swimming" is only telling you to rearrange DEEP NEXT.
annotation.definitionFit: Expedient means suitable or advantageous in the circumstances.

entries.clue: Same rare quality’s captured (5)

indicatorNotes.captured: the answer is held prisoner inside the words

annotation.surface: Two people share an uncommon trait, and both have been caught.
annotation.walkthrough: "Captured" looks like part of a crime story; it only says the answer is held inside the neighbouring words.
annotation.definitionFit: Equal means the same in amount or value.

entries.clue: European probe reported? (5)

indicatorNotes.reported?: a report is spoken, so we want a word that sounds like the next one

blocks.note: a probe is a check or examination

annotation.surface: News of a European investigation.
annotation.walkthrough: "European probe" reads as an inquiry run by Europe; European is in fact the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A Czech is a person from the Czech Republic, in Europe.

entries.clue: Praise adult I trained on piano (7)

indicatorNotes.trained: training shapes something, so the letters are reshaped into a new order
indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, putting one thing on another sets it after, so P comes first

annotation.surface: A grown-up learner earns compliments for their piano playing.
annotation.walkthrough: "Trained on piano" reads as music lessons; it actually reshuffles ADULT I and sets the result after P.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: praise here is the noun, and plaudit is a formal word for applause or acclaim.

entries.clue: Ultimately hilarious punning in cutting performance? (9)

indicatorNotes.Ultimately: in the end, so take the final letter

annotation.surface: A comedian's act, full of very funny puns, that cuts deep.
annotation.walkthrough: "Cutting performance" sounds like a sharp comic turn, but it means a fencing display, hence the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: Swordplay is the skill or display of fencing with swords, a performance with blades.

entries.clue: Remarkably valiant European (7)

indicatorNotes.Remarkably: the letters are arranged in a remarkable, unusual way

annotation.surface: Praise for a very brave person from Europe.
annotation.walkthrough: Reads as "a remarkably brave European"; VALIANT holds exactly the letters of the nationality.
annotation.definitionFit: A Latvian is a person from Latvia, in Europe.

entries.clue: Further back (6)

blocks.note: a verb: to help a cause along
a verb: to support, as a motion at a meeting

annotation.walkthrough: "Further back" reads as a direction, farther behind; split it into two verbs that each mean to support. To second a motion is to formally support it.
annotation.definitionFit: Double definition from the meeting-room sense: supporting a proposal both furthers it and backs it.

entries.clue: Beginning to sense fish smell badly (6)

annotation.definitionNote: "smell badly" stands for the noun a bad smell

indicatorNotes.Beginning to: take the first letter of the next word

annotation.surface: Starting to notice that fish smells off.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads "smell" as a verb; the answer is the noun, a bad smell.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym once "smell" is read as a noun: an odour that is bad is exactly what the answer names.

entries.clue: Test applied, odd parts ignored for instance (7)

indicatorNotes.odd parts ignored: drop the letters in odd positions and keep the even ones

annotation.surface: An exam question where odd sections are skipped, for instance.
annotation.walkthrough: "For instance" looks like a single phrase; "for" is the link and "instance" alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a case in point, as in "for instance" and "for example" being interchangeable.

entries.clue: Slice pastry, case unfilled (5)

indicatorNotes.unfilled: with the filling gone, only the outside letters remain

annotation.surface: A slice of pie whose pastry case has no filling.
annotation.walkthrough: The empty pastry case fits the bakery picture, but "unfilled" is telling you to empty the word CASE.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a portion cut from a cake or pie can be called either word.

entries.clue: Characteristic of revolutionary paintings etc with it (5)

indicatorNotes.revolutionary: a revolution turns something round, so the letters run backwards

annotation.surface: A trademark of radical, avant-garde art that is fashionable.
annotation.walkthrough: "Revolutionary paintings" suggests daring art; revolutionary only turns ART round.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: characteristic is the noun here, a distinguishing quality, not the adjective.

entries.clue: Oil for cooking half of very green fruit? (5)

indicatorNotes.for cooking: cooked ingredients are changed, so the letters are mixed up
indicatorNotes.half of: take the first half of the word

blocks.note: the first two of VERY's four letters

annotation.surface: A cooking oil made from half-ripe green fruit.
annotation.walkthrough: Olive oil is exactly the kitchen scene, but "oil for cooking" is only OIL rearranged; the question mark admits olives are not always green.
annotation.definitionFit: An olive is a small fruit, often eaten green.

entries.clue: Versatile kitchen set (7)

indicatorNotes.Versatile: versatile things turn every way, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A multipurpose set of kitchen utensils.
annotation.walkthrough: "Kitchen set" suggests a pan set; "set" is the verb, as a sauce or jelly sets.
annotation.definitionFit: When a jelly or sauce sets, it thickens.

entries.clue: Sweet piece of music entertaining lower classes, primarily (6)

indicatorNotes.entertaining: entertaining someone means having them in, so DUET holds the letters
indicatorNotes.primarily: take the first letter of each word

blocks.note: a piece for two performers, split as DU...ET
first letters of lower and classes

annotation.surface: A pleasant song performed for working-class audiences.
annotation.walkthrough: "Lower classes" is not a social group here: only its initials go inside DUET.
annotation.definitionFit: Dulcet means sweet and soothing, usually of a sound.

entries.clue: Pilfer handful of notes (6)

blocks.note: a short fragment of a song

annotation.surface: A thief grabs a fistful of banknotes.
annotation.walkthrough: "Notes" suggests money, fitting the theft, but here they are musical notes: a snatch of a tune.
annotation.definitionFit: To snatch is to steal, and a snatch is a brief bit of music.
